title: Noisy Quantum Query Complexity via Fractional Block Sensitivity
authors: Mehil Agarwal, Shravas Rao, Fang Song
abstract: We study quantum query complexity under several models of imperfect oracle access, and develop lower bounds through a common framework based on fractional block sensitivity (\(\fbs\)).   For a negligent oracle that applies the correct query with probability \(1-p\), we prove a lower bound in terms of \(\fbs(f,0^n)\). We also show, perhaps surprisingly, that negligence need not destroy quantum speedups: any function \(f\) can be transformed into a partial function \(f'\) whose negligent query complexity essentially preserves the quantum query complexity of \(f\). This gives partial functions with exponential quantum speedups even under negligent queries, and in particular rules out a general lower bound in terms of \(\fbs(f)\) for partial functions in this model.   For two other models, we obtain general lower bounds in terms of \(\fbs(f)\) for all Boolean functions. For hybrid algorithms using \(Q\) coherent and \(C\) classical queries, we prove the tradeoff \(C+Q^2=Ω(\fbs(f))\). For an IID dephasing noisy model where each query dephases the query-index register at rate \(p\) independently, we prove \(Ω\!\left(p\,\fbs(f)\right)\) queries are necessary.   Finally, we introduce a broader family of time-varying dephasing models and identify a variational resource that is always lower bounded by \(\fbs(f)\). Computing this resource reduces to a convex optimization problem, providing a simple way to derive lower bounds for new noise schedules. As applications, we recover the hybrid and IID dephasing bounds and determine the query complexity of unstructured search when the dephasing rate grows over time.
summary: This paper develops a unified theoretical framework using fractional block sensitivity to determine the quantum query complexity of functions under various forms of noise. It derives specific lower bounds for negligent and dephasing noise models, culminating in a general 'Computational-Opportunity Theorem.' This work is significant for understanding the fundamental limits of quantum computation when faced with realistic imperfections.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum query complexity for functions under various models of imperfect oracle access, including negligent and dephasing noise.
main_result: They establish lower bounds for quantum query complexity in terms of fractional block sensitivity (fbs) for multiple noise models, including a novel 'Computational-Opportunity Theorem' for time-varying dephasing.
method: The core method involves developing a unified framework based on fractional block sensitivity (fbs) and applying it to analyze resource constraints imposed by different noise processes.
model_or_system: The study analyzes abstract computational models involving oracle queries, specifically considering the impact of noise characterized by negligence probability (p) or time-dependent dephasing rates (p_t).
key_observables: Quantum query complexity ($Q_\epsilon(f)$), fractional block sensitivity ($	ext{fbs}(f)$), and the derived 'opportunity resource function' ($R(\mu)$).
important_parameters: Noise probabilities ($p, p_t$), error tolerance ($\epsilon$), and the structure of the function $f$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on establishing lower bounds by relating quantum resources to the fbs, and in the extended dephasing model, it assumes the resource can be characterized by a convex optimization problem.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by introducing fbs, applying it sequentially to the negligent model, the hybrid query model, the IID dephasing model, and finally generalizing to a comprehensive 'Computational-Opportunity Theorem' for time-varying dephasing schedules.
why_interesting: The development of the Computational-Opportunity Theorem provides a powerful, general tool to derive lower bounds for quantum algorithms operating in realistic, noisy physical environments, bridging theoretical complexity with physical noise models.
